extraction.name: The LAMBADA dataset: Word prediction requiring a broad discourse context
extraction.description: LAMBADA is a dataset to evaluate the capabilities of computational models for text understanding by means of a word prediction task. It consists of narrative passages where human subjects can guess the last word if they see the whole passage, but not if they only see the last sentence. The dataset aims to test models' ability to use broader discourse context.
extraction.creator: Denis Papemo, Germán Kruszewski, Angeliki Lazaridou, Quan Ngoc Pham, Raffaella Bernardi, Sandro Pezzelle, Marco Baroni, Gemma Boleda, Raquel Fernández
extraction.citeAs: Papemo, D., Kruszewski, G., Lazaridou, A., Pham, Q. N., Bernardi, R., Pezzelle, S., Baroni, M., Boleda, G., & Fernández, R. (2016). The LAMBADA dataset: Word prediction requiring a broad discourse context. Proceedings of the 54th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics, 1525–1534.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Passages were extracted from the Book Corpus (Zhu et al., 2015), which contains unpublished novels. The corpus after duplicate removal and filtering contains 5,325 novels and 465 million words. Novels were randomly divided into training and development+testing partitions. Passages were filtered using language models and human evaluation via CrowdFlower.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Book Corpus (Zhu et al., 2015) - a collection of unpublished novels.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Duplicate removal and filtering out of potentially offensive material with a stop word list. Passages were filtered using language models to exclude those where the target word had probability >=0.00175 according to any of four language models. Then human evaluation steps were conducted.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human subjects guessed the target word via CrowdFlower in three steps: (1) guess based on whole passage; if correct, (2) another subject guesses based on whole passage; if correct, (3) up to 10 subjects guess based on target sentence only. Passages were included only if two consecutive subjects guessed correctly in broad context and no subject guessed correctly from sentence alone.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Subjects were allowed 3 guesses per sentence in step 3. Step 2 was added to ensure data were easy given discourse context. It was ensured that the same subject could not judge the same item in both passage and sentence conditions.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 2 (for broad context) and up to 10 (for sentence context)
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Language models used for filtering: pre-trained RNN, 4-gram model, RNN, feed-forward model (all trained on Book Corpus).
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The development set and training corpus are available for download. The test set will be made available at the time of a planned public competition.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset has a bias towards proper nouns (48% of target words) and common nouns (37%). Verbs, adjectives, and adverbs are rare. The dataset also contains more direct speech than input items.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is challenging for current models; none of the tested models achieved accuracy above 1%. The strict inclusion criteria (exact match of target word) may exclude passages with plausible synonyms. The dataset is limited to English and to the novel genre.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation. The dataset is intended to evaluate language models' ability to use broad discourse context. The training data (2662 novels, 203M words) can be used for unsupervised training. The development set can be used for fine-tuning.
